## 2024-06-17 - Fix XSS in History Loading
**Vulnerability:** The `loadHistory` function in `index.html` was susceptible to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS). It reconstructed the UI from JSON stored in `localStorage` by directly interpolating the `url` property into the `innerHTML` string (`<img src="${item.url}" ...>`) without sanitization or properly escaping quotes.
**Learning:** Even when inputs are considered "internal" (like local storage history generated by the application itself), dynamically generating HTML strings using `innerHTML` with unsanitized properties creates a severe XSS vector if any path allows an attacker to control the stored value. Single quotes are not escaped when stringified/parsed normally unless deliberately handled.
**Prevention:** Avoid `innerHTML` for DOM construction when dealing with dynamic or potentially tainted data. Instead, leverage the safe DOM API (e.g., `document.createElement`) and direct property assignments (`img.src = item.url`), which automatically treat the input as data rather than executable HTML context.
